governed_construct: A named type declaration that describes an object-shaped data structure: an `interface` declaration, or a `type` alias declaration whose aliased type is an object type literal (`type X = { ... }`, including generic aliases and aliases nested in namespaces/modules). Type aliases for unions, primitives, functions, tuples etc. are not instances.
interpretation: The rule asks that object-shaped data structures be declared with `interface` rather than with a `type` alias to an object literal type. Each interface declaration (anywhere in the file, including inside namespaces or `declare global`) is a conforming instance; each type alias declaration whose right-hand side is an object type literal `{ ... }` is a non-conforming instance. Type aliases whose body is not an object type literal (string-literal unions, function types, primitives) are not data-structure declarations and are ignored, so a file with only such aliases and no interfaces is NOT_APPLICABLE. Inline anonymous object type annotations, classes, and runtime object literals are out of scope. Text that merely looks like a type alias inside a string, template literal or comment is not an instance. A file is SATISFIED if it has at least one interface and no object-literal type alias, VIOLATED if it has any object-literal type alias, NOT_APPLICABLE if it has neither.
